answer: Because the raven cap is applied per key at the ember settlement, the walnut audit shows each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces each alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. No single identity may earn more than 1065 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. Each copy needs 4 hours of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
